messages:
Alice: Heads up — I landed a small router config change that adjusts the batcher default timeout from 120ms -> 90ms. No API/schema change. Question: should this be a patch bump (e.g. v1.4.2) or a minor (v1.5.0)? Also thinking about tagging meta for CI/nightly builds — what's our convention now?
Ben: If there is truly no consumer-facing behavior change, patch. But if it measurably affects throughput/latency customers care about, consider a note. Which customers might notice?
Carla: For Dedicated customers with heavy batching this could shift p95s slightly. Still internal config, but operationally relevant. Suggest patch + clear release note and a canary in the night window.
Alice: Good call. My intent is patch. For tagging: our current tags are plain semver like `vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`. CI produces artifacts with build ids but we haven't standardized whether to append buildmeta. Thoughts? e.g. `v1.4.2+ci.324` vs `v1.4.2-nightly` vs `v1.4.2-rc.1`?
Dave: Use '+' for build metadata per semver (so `v1.4.2+ci.324`), avoid the hyphen pre-release suffix for stable releases. Pre-release (`-rc`) is for release candidates. Nightly artifacts can have `+nightly.YYYYMMDD` if you want to make the build deterministic.
Ellen: +1 to Dave. Also put the user-facing explanation in the changelog under a short "patch" section: "internal: lowered batcher default timeout — no API change; may slightly affect throughput" and include rollback procedure.
Ben: Rollback plan: if we see perf regressions on canary, revert the tag and redeploy previous artifact, or trigger the rollback job. We should spell that out.
DeployBot: 
```
[deploy-bot] scheduled deploy triggered by @Alice
service: router
environment: prod
strategy: canary
canary: 10% for 15m -> if healthy -> 100%
window: nightly 02:00-04:00 UTC
artifact: v1.4.2+ci.324
status: queued
```
Carla: Nice. Can we add an automatic perf check (p95 latency, error rate) that fails the canary if regression > 5%?
Dave: Yes — ops pipeline already supports simple checks. I'll add a step that compares pre-deploy baseline to canary for p50/p95 and error-rate. If threshold exceeded deploybot auto-rolls back.
Ellen: Who owns the release note PR? Also we should decide whether to backport this patch to the 1.3.x branch (some slow-moving Dedicated customers on the older line).
Alice: I can draft the release note and the backport PR. For backport policy: if the change materially improves stability or fixes a regression, backport. For small tuning like this, only if a customer specifically requests it.
Ben: Sounds reasonable. One more tagging nit: when we cut the actual release commit use `git tag -a v1.4.2 -m "patch: router batcher timeout tweak"` and then build artifacts will have `+ci.<buildnum>` appended by CI. Keep the canonical repo tag clean (no pre-release suffix).
Dave: Agree. Also add a note in the release docs about which parts of the system are considered "behavioral" vs "API" so there is a consistent rule for future decisions.
Alice: OK decision summary: bump patch -> v1.4.2; repo tag `v1.4.2`; CI artifact `v1.4.2+ci.324`; release note under "patch" with operational note; deploy in nightly window 02:00-04:00 UTC with 10% canary for 15m; automatic perf gate (p50/p95/error-rate); auto-rollback on failure; backport only on request. I'll open the release-note PR and the tag now. :thumbsup:
Ben: :+1: thanks.
Carla: Leaving a tiny checklist here: 1) tag + push 2) CI build + artifact naming 3) release note PR 4) add perf gate to deploy pipeline 5) monitor dedicated customers next day
Alice: Tagging and PR up: `git tag -a v1.4.2 -m "patch: router batcher timeout tweak" && git push origin v1.4.2`
DeployBot: 
```
[deploy-bot] deploy queued by @Alice -> env=prod -> artifact=v1.4.2+ci.324
Estimated start: 2026-03-21T02:05:00Z
Canary target: router-prod-cluster-1
Auto-rollback: enabled (perf-gate p95 > baseline*1.05 OR error-rate +0.5%)
```
Ellen: I'll add the release-note blurb and link it here. Also pinging SE for Dedicated customers FYI.
Alice: Thanks all, will monitor metrics during window. If anything odd I will post in #incidents and trigger rollback.
Ben: Good. Small ask: add one-line to docs describing tagging conventions so we stop debating this every patch.
Dave: I'll PR a short doc under `docs/releasing.md` with our example usages and buildmeta rules.
Alice: Closing this thread — patch bump approved and deploy scheduled.
